headline: Medium pairwise risks: shared customer-data workflows and allowlisted egress create leakage and cascading-error exposure; prompt injection and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot ingests messages and supports integrations, while Cognee operates as a memory/CLI system with session memory. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, if Chatwoot content is copied or piped into Cognee, attacker-controlled text could influence downstream prompts. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is manually copied into Cognee prompts or files, injection content can propagate.
IF an operator connects both through a shared workspace or clipboard bridge, untrusted text may be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Require explicit prompt delimiters for any Chatwoot-to-Cognee transfer.
Strip markup and instructions from copied support text before reuse.
Use a read-only export step for Chatwoot transcripts.
Add a short operator checklist for untrusted content handling.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and orders; Cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history. Both have network egress, and Cognee can call external services via API keys. A shared workspace is not documented, but the pair can still leak sensitive support data if Chatwoot content is fed into Cognee for memory or analysis.
conditions: IF Chatwoot transcripts or customer records are imported into Cognee, sensitive data enters a second system.
IF Cognee is configured with external API keys, stored support data may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Limit imports to redacted samples.
Disable external API keys during support-data testing.
Separate production customer data from Cognee indexes.
Review outbound destinations before enabling sync.
Use a short-lived staging workspace for transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot exposes integrations and broad egress, while Cognee uses CLI tooling with session-scoped memory and supports multiple instances. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same filesystem, database, or OAuth scopes, so direct conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because the shared target resource is undocumented, so the safer low severity is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable backend, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator shares a single state directory without locking, concurrent updates may collide.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same backend.
Enable locking in the orchestrator if shared state is unavoidable.
Schedule sequential runs for mutable tasks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces support conversations and reports, and Cognee stores decisions, workflows, and successful implementations. That makes a plausible chain where Chatwoot output becomes Cognee input and Cognee later reuses it as authoritative memory. No verification step is documented, so errors or hallucinations can cascade across the pair in default support workflows.
conditions: IF Chatwoot summaries are ingested into Cognee without review, incorrect facts can persist.
IF Cognee-generated recommendations are reused in support workflows, downstream actions may amplify errors.
mitigations: Require human review before indexing Chatwoot summaries.
Tag imported items with source and timestamp.
Keep generated recommendations separate from factual records.
Add a verification step before any customer-facing action.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Cognee touches personal data and finance data. The profiles do not document residency or certification alignment, so a compliance mismatch cannot be ruled out. Because both systems can process regulated data classes and the interaction is undocumented, the conservative choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF EU personal data is moved from Chatwoot into a US-hosted Cognee deployment without a DPA, residency risk arises.
IF regulated customer records are indexed in Cognee without matching retention controls, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Confirm data residency for both deployments.
Map retention settings before syncing records.
Exclude regulated fields from Cognee indexes.
Document a DPA or equivalent transfer basis.
Run a quick compliance review on the shared data classes.
